label: copy-phase update gate, favoring inputs c/m/a/d/x/p/o/3 at mid-sequence recall positions
predicate: (phase == 2) & (recall_idx >= 2) & isin(in_tok, [tok("c"), tok("m"), tok("a"), tok("d"), tok("x"), tok("p"), tok("o"), tok("3")])
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, never on original inputs or the <DEL> step; essentially all of it falls at recall_idx >= 2 (outputs 1 to 6 steps from the end), with the highest rates at recall_idx 4-5 / t 11-13. Inside the copy phase it is sparse (about 12% of steps) and depends on the token: input c is strongest (20% rate, 17% of mass), then m, with a/d/x/p/o/3 above baseline; output tokens c/e/z/t give a weaker lift. The largest activations are in short L=3 sequences when the second original token (often c, m or d) is fed back. The token-set predicate gets about 0.32 precision and 0.59 recall (0.66 mass recall) on dev. The rest looks like it depends on sequence context in ways the per-step variables do not capture, so this is only a partial explanation.
